stories.headline: China hits 10 US firms with export controls and bars 46 from procurement in retaliation for Pentagon list

key_facts.fact: China's Ministry of Commerce added 10 US entities to its export control list on Monday, prohibiting exports of dual-use items to them effective immediately.
key_facts.excerpt: China's Ministry of Commerce announced Monday that it has decided to add 10 U.S. entities, including Aveox, Inc., to the export control list in accordance with the nation's export control law and regulations on export control of dual-use items.

key_facts.fact: The 10 firms include Aveox, Red Cat Holdings, Teal Drones, IMSAR, Jaia Robotics, Ball Aerospace & Technologies, Oshkosh Defense, L3Harris Maritime Services, MP Materials and USA Rare Earth.
key_facts.excerpt: Effective as of the date of this announcement, export operators are prohibited from exporting dual-use items to the 10 entities that also include Red Cat Holdings, Inc., Teal Drones, Inc., IMSAR, Jaia Robotics, Inc., Ball Aerospace & Technologies Corp., Oshkosh Defense, L3Harris Maritime Services, Inc., MP Materials Corp., and USA Rare Earth, Inc.

key_facts.fact: China's Finance Ministry separately barred government entities from buying products from 46 US companies, including multiple units of Lockheed Martin, Raytheon and General Dynamics.
key_facts.excerpt: Separately, the Finance Ministry said that government entities would be prohibited from buying products from 46 American companies including multiple units of Lockheed Martin, Raytheon and General Dynamics.

key_facts.fact: Beijing framed the move as retaliation for the US Defense Department's expansion of the Section 1260H 'Chinese military companies' list, which added Alibaba, BYD, Baidu, NIO, CALB Group and Unitree Robotics earlier this month.
key_facts.excerpt: The move comes less than two weeks after the US Defense Department expanded its list of what it describes as Chinese military companies under Section 1260H of the National Defense Authorization Act. Major Chinese technology and manufacturing firms including Alibaba, BYD, Nio, CALB Group and Unitree Robotics have all been added to the list.

key_facts.fact: MP Materials operates the only active rare earth mine in the US (Mountain Pass, California); USA Rare Earth is the other anchor of Washington's domestic rare earth push.
key_facts.excerpt: MP Materials operates the Mountain Pass mine in California — the only active rare earth mining and processing facility in the US — and USA Rare Earth anchors Washington's push for domestic production. Both now face restricted access to Chinese dual-use exports, adding friction to the US strategy they're meant to underpin.

key_facts.fact: Han Shen Lin of The Asia Group told CNBC the action is 'largely symbolic' since most listed firms do little China business; the 1260H procurement ban takes effect on June 30.
key_facts.excerpt: Han Shen Lin, China country director at The Asia Group, told CNBC the move is 'largely symbolic,' noting most listed companies do little actual business in China. The 1260H list that triggered Beijing's response carries no automatic sanctions — it bars US government agencies from buying products made by listed Chinese companies, with that ban taking effect June 30.

key_facts.fact: US-funded enterprises operating inside China are exempted from the procurement ban; companies may apply for licences for goods 'genuinely necessary'.
key_facts.excerpt: However, companies operating in China through locally invested entities would be exempt from the procurement ban.

stories.headline: WiseTech shares plunge 18% after report Australian Federal Police probe founder Richard White over trafficking and visa-fraud claims

key_facts.fact: WiseTech Global shares fell 18.4% on Monday to A$30.08, the lowest closing level since early June 2021, after reports the Australian Federal Police is investigating executive chairman Richard White.
key_facts.excerpt: Shares of the logistics software firm fell 18.4% to A$30.08, the lowest closing level since early June 2021. The stock was the top loser in the ASX200 benchmark index, which closed down 0.1%.

key_facts.fact: The AFP's human exploitation taskforce is examining allegations that White exploited a woman's immigration status for sex and provided false information on a visa application, the Australian Financial Review reported.
key_facts.excerpt: According to articles in the Sydney Morning Herald and the Australian Financial Review, the Australian Federal Police's human exploitation taskforce has started a probe into White after a complaint.

key_facts.fact: The complaint to the AFP came from Kathy Phelan, former CEO of Kyckr, a separate White-controlled company, and alleges White made up a reason to hire a woman once employed as a cleaner at WiseTech and supplied false visa information.
key_facts.excerpt: The AFR article and others said the federal police launched an investigation into White, WiseTech's billionaire founder, this year after a complaint from the former head of Kyckr, a separate company controlled by White. The complaint alleged White made up a reason to hire a woman once employed by WiseTech as a cleaner, and provided false information to the government to get her a visa.

key_facts.fact: The selloff wiped about A$1.8 billion from WiseTech's market value on the day; the stock is down ~75% from its July 2025 peak around A$121.
key_facts.excerpt: Its share price was down just over 14.5 per cent by about 2.30pm, wiping about $1.8 billion from the company's value... It has lost almost 75 per cent of its value since soaring to about $121 per share in July last year.

key_facts.fact: White stepped down as CEO in late 2024 after a string of personal-life controversies, then returned as executive chairman in February 2026 after a boardroom cleanout.
key_facts.excerpt: White stepped down in late 2024 as chief executive officer after a string of allegations of misconduct, only to retake the helm as executive chairman months later after a boardroom cleanout.

key_facts.fact: The same woman, described as Brazilian and identified as Caroline Heidemann, previously made similar allegations and reached a private settlement with White, according to Sky News.
key_facts.excerpt: WiseTech's founder Richard White is alleged to have provided false information to the government to get his former employee and romantic partner Caroline Heidemann a visa, according to The Australian Financial Review. Mr White allegedly used his power to coerce the Brazilian Ms Heidemann into a relationship. She has reached a settlement with the billionaire.

stories.headline: Defense tech startups have raised $12.3B in 2026 already, surpassing all of 2025 — Anduril took half

key_facts.fact: Defense technology startups worldwide raised $12.3 billion from venture capital so far in 2026, nearly double the same period last year and already past 2025's full-year total of $9.95 billion, per PitchBook data cited by the Financial Times.
key_facts.excerpt: According to the Financial Times (FT) of the U.K. and global market research firm PitchBook on the 22nd (local time), defense technology startups worldwide have raised $12.3 billion (about 18.8 trillion won) from VCs so far this year. That is nearly double the same period last year. They surpassed the full-year total investment of $9.95 billion in less than half a year.

key_facts.fact: US startups captured $11.4 billion of the $12.3 billion (93%); nearly half of the global total went to Anduril Industries.
key_facts.excerpt: PitchBook data show that U.S. startups captured $11.4 billion, or 93%, of the $12.3 billion in total defense technology investment in the first half of this year. Nearly half of that went to Anduril Industries.

key_facts.fact: Anduril raised an additional $5 billion last month, nearly doubling its valuation in a year to $61 billion; investors include Thrive Capital and Andreessen Horowitz.
key_facts.excerpt: The company raised an additional $5 billion just last month, nearly doubling its valuation in a year to $61 billion. The investor list includes Thrive Capital, which led investment in OpenAI, and Andreessen Horowitz, one of the world's largest VCs.

key_facts.fact: Investor interest is shifting from heavy hardware to 'asymmetric' cheap, mass-producible weapons — drones, autonomous surface vessels, battlefield AI — after Ukraine and Middle East conflicts showcased their effectiveness.
key_facts.excerpt: Global investors are pouring money into defense technology startups — drones, autonomous vessels and battlefield AI systems — as the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East drag on. Venture capital flowing into defense tech startups worldwide in the first half of this year has already surpassed the full-year total for 2025.

key_facts.fact: Mikolaj Firlej, co-founder of European defense-focused VC Expeditions, says drones may be overcrowded but autonomous maritime systems, military satellites and battlefield AI remain in early growth.
key_facts.excerpt: 'If the first wave of investment was about restoring weapons production capacity, we are now moving into a race to secure supply chains and advanced technology,' said Mikolaj Firlej, co-founder of Expeditions, a European defense-focused venture capital firm. 'Sensors, electronic warfare and battlefield AI will be the core investment areas for years to come.'

stories.headline: Anduril explores Israel operations, courting Elbit and DDR&D candidates for local manager

key_facts.fact: Anduril is exploring an Israeli expansion and in talks to recruit a local manager to build ties with Israeli startups and identify partnership opportunities, Calcalist reported.
key_facts.excerpt: Anduril, the world's largest and most closely watched defense startup, has begun exploring the possibility of establishing operations in Israel. According to information obtained by Calcalist, the company is currently in talks to recruit a local manager who would be tasked with building relationships with Israeli startups and identifying partnership opportunities.

key_facts.fact: Meetings in recent weeks were held with potential candidates from Elbit Systems and the Directorate of Defense Research and Development (DDR&D) at Israel's Ministry of Defense.
key_facts.excerpt: To that end, meetings have been held in recent weeks with potential candidates from Elbit Systems and the Directorate of Defense Research and Development at Israel's Ministry of Defense (DDR&D).

key_facts.fact: Anduril is also weighing setting up a local R&D operation and hiring Israeli employees; the local arm would handle sales to the Israeli Ministry of Defense and R&D for global products.
key_facts.excerpt: Innovative US military technology company Anduril Industries, which raised money recently at a $61 billion valuation, is currently meeting with a number of senior officials in Israel to establish a local operation that will deal with sales to the Ministry of Defense and R&D for its global products, 'Globes' has learned.

key_facts.fact: Founder Palmer Luckey — who has described himself as a 'radical Zionist' — visited Israel in February on a trip organized by Lux Capital's Josh Wolfe that included a meeting with PM Benjamin Netanyahu.
key_facts.excerpt: In February, Luckey, who has previously described himself as a 'radical Zionist,' visited Israel. The trip, organized by Josh Wolfe, founder of venture capital firm Lux Capital and one of Anduril's earliest investors, included a meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

key_facts.fact: Anduril has already signed agreements with several Israeli startups, including ASIO, which is expected to supply components for Anduril's unmanned aerial systems.
key_facts.excerpt: Anduril has already signed agreements with several Israeli companies, including ASIO, which is expected to supply components for the company's unmanned aerial systems.

stories.headline: Iran reshuts Strait of Hormuz as Vance opens first US–Iran talks under June MoU; Trump threatens fresh strikes

key_facts.fact: Vice President JD Vance led the first US–Iran talks under the June interim peace deal on Sunday at the Qatari-owned Bürgenstock resort in Switzerland, extending the April ceasefire by at least 60 days.
key_facts.excerpt: The talks in the Qatari-owned Swiss mountaintop resort of Buergenstock were the first to be held under the terms of a memorandum of understanding reached between the two enemies last week to end their war, extending a tenuous ceasefire from April for at least another 60 days.

key_facts.fact: While talks opened, Trump threatened on Truth Social to hit Iran 'very hard again, just like we did last week, only harder' if Tehran did not stop Hezbollah 'proxies' in Lebanon.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Iran must immediately stop their highly paid PROXIES in Lebanon from causing trouble,' Trump wrote on social media, apparently referring to Iran's Hezbollah allies in Lebanon. 'If they don't, we'll hit Iran very hard again, just like we did last week, only harder!!!'

key_facts.fact: Iran announced on Saturday it had again closed the Strait of Hormuz, citing continued Israeli strikes on Lebanon and US 'bad faith'; the previous closure caused 'the biggest disruption of global energy supplies in history'.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran said on June 20 that as a result, it had again shut the strait, whose closure for nearly four months caused the biggest disruption of global energy supplies in history.

key_facts.fact: A US diplomat told Axios that the parties made 'good progress' on keeping Hormuz open and discussed enforcing the Lebanon ceasefire and the nuclear deal during the talks.
key_facts.excerpt: Late on Sunday, a US diplomat told Axios that during the talks the parties had made good progress on keeping the Strait of Hormuz open. The talks also focused on enforcing the ceasefire in Lebanon as well as the nuclear deal, the US diplomat told Axios.

key_facts.fact: Israel killed at least 29–30 people across southern Lebanon on Saturday, a day after a fresh Israel–Hezbollah ceasefire; total Lebanese death toll since the March 2 offensive exceeds 4,000.
key_facts.excerpt: Israeli attacks on Lebanon have continued in the days since the MoU's signing, bringing the death toll since the start of Israel's air and ground offensive on March 2 to more than 4,000.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude opened Monday up more than $1 to $82.30 on the new Hormuz closure, then slid to $79.04 (-1.90%) as Iran said it had secured waivers for oil and petrochemical exports.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude fell $1.53, or 1.90%, to $79.04 a barrel by 0656 GMT. Prices had earlier climbed to $82.30 at the start of trading, fuelled by a bumpy start to the talks with threats from U.S. President Donald Trump to restart the war on Iran and Tehran's announcement it had again closed the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: Europe heatwave pushes France to 42°C and UK toward 38°C record as red alerts widen

key_facts.fact: France placed 35 of its 96 mainland departments under the highest 'red' heat alert on Sunday June 21, with the number expected to rise to 49 on Monday; temperatures up to 41°C forecast.
key_facts.excerpt: France implemented some of Europe's strictest measures after placing 35 of its 96 mainland departments under the highest 'red' heat alert on Sunday, with the number expected to rise to 49 on Monday. ... of up to 41 degrees Celsius (105.8 degrees Fahrenheit) were forecast in

key_facts.fact: 42.2°C was recorded in Pissos, southwest France on Sunday; France banned alcohol in red-alert areas and cancelled outdoor sports as wildfire alerts were issued to emergency services and the military.
key_facts.excerpt: In some parts of the country, temperatures had already passed the 40-degree mark, with 42.2 degrees recorded in Pissos, in the southwest Landes region.

key_facts.fact: UK Met Office issued a four-day amber 'extreme heat' warning through Thursday with forecasts reaching 38°C — just under the all-time June record of 35.6°C set in 1976.
key_facts.excerpt: A four-day amber weather warning for extreme heat has taken effect, with forecasts suggesting temperatures could reach 38C (100F) in parts of England this week. The Met Office warning is in place until 23:59 BST on Thursday

key_facts.fact: Spain declared its first official heatwave of the year from Sunday through Wednesday with temperatures forecast to hit 44°C in some regions.
key_facts.excerpt: Spain declared its first official heat wave of the year from Sunday through Wednesday, with temperatures forecast to reach 44C (111.2F) in parts of the country.

key_facts.fact: Italy expanded 'red flag' heat alerts to eight northern and central cities including Bologna, Florence, Milan and Turin.
key_facts.excerpt: After several days of temperatures above 35 deg C, Italian authorities issued a red alert for June 21 in eight cities, including Bologna, Florence, Milan and Turin.

key_facts.fact: WHO Europe says more than 200,000 people across Europe died from heat-related causes over the last four years; an attribution study said human-caused climate change killed about 1,500 people in an early May 2026 heatwave.
key_facts.excerpt: Over the last four years, more than 200,000 people across Europe died from heat-related causes, and most of the fatalities were preventable, the World Health Organization's Europe office said this month. ... A rapid study found that human-caused climate change was responsible for killing about 1,500 people in an unusually early European heat wave in May.

stories.headline: FDA approves GSK and Spero's Utebzi as the first oral carbapenem antibiotic for complicated UTIs

key_facts.fact: The US FDA approved Utebzi (tebipenem pivoxil) for complicated urinary tract infections including pyelonephritis in adults with limited or no alternative oral options — the first and only oral carbapenem cleared for this indication.
key_facts.excerpt: GSK plc (LSE/NYSE: GSK) and Spero Therapeutics (Nasdaq: SPRO) today announced that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Utebzi, an oral antibiotic for the treatment of complicated urinary tract infections (cUTIs) including pyelonephritis, caused by certain susceptible pathogens in adult patients who have limited or no alternative oral treatment options. This is the first and only oral carbapenem antibiotic approved for these patients.

key_facts.fact: Approval is based on the global Phase III PIVOT-PO non-inferiority trial that enrolled 1,690 patients, comparing oral tebipenem 600 mg q6h to IV imipenem-cilastatin 500 mg q6h for 7–10 days.
key_facts.excerpt: The PIVOT-PO trial was a global, randomised, double-blind, pivotal, non-inferiority (NI margin: -10%) phase III trial evaluating the potential of oral tebipenem pivoxil compared to IV imipenem-cilastatin, in hospitalised adult patients with complicated urinary tract infections, including acute pyelonephritis. ... The trial enrolled a total of 1,690 patients

key_facts.fact: The clearance follows a 2022 FDA rejection of Spero's original ADAPT-PO data and a redesigned pivotal study; Spero restructured significantly after the setback before licensing the asset to GSK.
key_facts.excerpt: The Food and Drug Administration concluded in 2022 that the original evidence was insufficient to support approval and requested another clinical trial. The setback contributed to a major restructuring at Spero Therapeutics and created uncertainty over whether the programme could continue.

key_facts.fact: The new oral option could let selected patients avoid or shorten intravenous antibiotic therapy for resistant UTIs, an outpatient-care shift for hospital-discharged patients.
key_facts.excerpt: The approval creates the first oral carbapenem option in the United States and could allow selected patients with susceptible infections to avoid or shorten intravenous antibiotic treatment.
